a viral blip of >200 copies/mL is a warning sign for viral rebound and should trigger an investigation for adherence issues.

blips of 500 copies/mL or greater are more likely to be associated with a subsequent rebound than blips of 200 copies/mL or less, and that the magnitude of blips may be associated with the risk of rebound.

the more sensitive the viral assay, the more blips and the higher the risk of viral breakthrough.
